result:
FINDING: app/auth.py:14 | SQL injection: `name` is interpolated into the query with an f-string. Use a parameterized query.
FINDING: app/auth.py:5 | Hardcoded signing secret in source. Load it from the environment or a secrets store.
FINDING: app/auth.py:21 | The password salt is the username, so it is predictable and not unique per user. Use a random per-user salt.
FINDING: app/auth.py:33 | The token is an HMAC of the user_id alone, with no expiry or nonce, so it never expires and can be replayed.
FINDING: app/files.py:10 | Path traversal in `export_report`: `filename` is not sanitized, so `../` or an absolute path writes outside EXPORT_DIR. `read_report` uses `basename`, but this function doesn't.
FINDING: app/orders.py:13 | Off-by-one: the docstring says $100.00 or more gets the discount, but `>` excludes exactly 10,000 cents. Use `>=`.
FINDING: app/orders.py:23 | Tax is computed on the undiscounted `subtotal`. The docstring says it is charged on the discounted amount, so it should use `discounted`.
FINDING: app/orders.py:61 | `place_order` ignores the return value of `reserve`. Each `reserve` commits on its own, and the checks and reserves are not atomic, so concurrent orders can oversell or leave a partial reservation. Check the result and wrap the whole order in one transaction.
FINDING: app/inventory.py:10 | Off-by-one in `paginate`: the slice end is `start + page_size - 1`, so each page returns only 9 items and every 10th item is dropped. Use `start + page_size`.
FINDING: app/inventory.py:23 | `reserve` has a check-then-update race and commits on its own, which breaks the atomicity `place_order` needs. Use a single conditional `UPDATE ... WHERE qty >= ?` and check `rowcount`.
FINDING: app/db.py:37 | `INSERT OR REPLACE` in `add_item` silently overwrites an existing item, which resets its stock and price. Use an explicit upsert or insert.
FINDING: app/orders.py:35 | `dedupe_skus` is O(n²) because it does a membership check on a list. Use a set alongside the list, or `dict.fromkeys`.
FINDING: app/orders.py:42 | `count_by_status` scans all orders once per status. It is also silently wrong for any status not in STATUSES. Use one pass with a `Counter`.
